options: A) Price is at its highest level
B) Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
questions.correct_answer: B) Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
questions.explanation: Market equilibrium is the point where Qd = Qs. At this price, there is no shortage and no surplus.

questions.text: Given Qd = 100 − 2P and Qs = 20 + 2P, what is the equilibrium price?
Using the same equations, what is the equilibrium quantity?
questions.explanation: Q* = 100 − 2(20) = 60 units. Both equations give the same answer.

questions.text: If price is ABOVE equilibrium, the result is:
questions.explanation: Above equilibrium: Qs > Qd → Surplus. Producers reduce prices to clear surplus.

questions.text: If price is BELOW equilibrium, the result is:
questions.explanation: Below equilibrium: Qd > Qs → Shortage. Consumers bid prices up.

questions.text: If DEMAND increases while supply stays the same, equilibrium price will:
questions.explanation: Demand shifts right → consumers want more at every price → prices bid up → equilibrium price increases.

questions.text: If SUPPLY increases while demand stays the same, equilibrium price will:
questions.explanation: Supply shifts right → more goods available → prices fall → equilibrium price decreases.

questions.text: A price ceiling set BELOW equilibrium will cause:
questions.explanation: Price ceiling below equilibrium → Qd > Qs → shortage, long queues, black markets.

questions.text: The 'invisible hand' that restores equilibrium refers to:
questions.explanation: Adam Smith's 'invisible hand' = market self-corrects through price changes without government.

questions.text: If BOTH demand and supply increase, the definite effect is:
questions.explanation: Both shift right → quantity definitely increases. Price effect is indeterminate.
